en.why_it_matters: This belongs because two place-based Black musical traditions are being asked to speak to each other on a DC stage. The Chuck Brown Band carries the continuous pocket and call-and-response grammar of go-go; Donald Harrison arrives not merely as a guest saxophonist but as a New Orleans culture keeper, with DCJF explicitly framing him as a soloist entering that rhythmic language. The hook is the collision of DC groove and Afro-New Orleans lineage in the festival finale, not the fame of either name.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for it if you are in the DMV: the hometown setting is part of the musical meaning, and this is the sort of festival collaboration worth catching in Washington rather than reading about afterward. I would not build a corridor trip solely around it, because the special billing is compelling without being documented as a farewell, premiere, or historically singular one-off.

El punto es ese cruce entre groove washingtoniano y linaje afro-neoorleanés en el cierre del festival, no el peso de los nombres por separado.

en.why_it_matters: The reason to care is the instrument and the room. Covington and LeDonne put two Hammond-organ voices at the center of a small guitar-and-drums setting inside Westminster's long-running Friday jazz tradition, turning the B-3's sustain, attack, bass movement, and church-to-soul-jazz vocabulary into the subject of the night. That is a specific DMV listening context, not just another festival slot.
en.trip_verdict: If Friday evening is open in the DMV, this is worth dropping into for the organ sound and the Westminster atmosphere. I would keep it as a strong local option rather than reorganizing the weekend around it, especially because the summit is explicitly a second edition rather than a one-time event.

es.why_it_matters: La razón para entrar es el instrumento y el lugar. Covington y LeDonne ponen dos voces de Hammond al centro de una formación pequeña con guitarra y batería dentro de la tradición de los viernes de jazz de Westminster; el sustain, el ataque, el bajo que construye el órgano y ese puente entre iglesia, soul jazz y groove se vuelven el tema de la noche. Es un contexto de escucha muy de DC, no una fecha genérica de festival.
es.trip_verdict: Si el viernes está libre en el DMV, vale caer por el sonido de los órganos y por la atmósfera de Westminster. Lo dejaría como una opción local muy buena, sin reorganizar el fin de semana alrededor de ella, especialmente porque el propio programa se presenta como una segunda edición y no como un one-off.
